subject: Frank Fly Brain 🦟, ByteDance Self-Improving AI 🔄, Bolt Open Model 💡
intro: Today's news shares a quiet theme: we're rethinking how AI learns, at every level. Sakana trains 1000-layer nets without backprop. ByteDance maps a 5-stage path to AI that rewrites itself. Bolt pays users in usage to crowdsource a trillion-parameter open model. Each story, in its own way, asks: what if the training process itself is the next frontier? news.headline: Frank wires a 166,700-neuron fruit fly brain model into a walking robot
news.body: Scientists at Google and HHMI Janelia just published the first complete wiring map of a fruit fly's nervous system: 166,700 neurons and 125 million connections . Think of it like a blueprint of every wire in a tiny biological computer. Someone took that blueprint, simulated it in software, and plugged it into a physical walking robot called a Strandbeest. The simulated brain's activity gets translated into motor commands that move the legs. Before this robot, the same brain played Doom and Chrome Dino. Here's the honest part: this is not a living brain. A connectome is a snapshot of dead wiring , not a mind. The simulation uses simplified neuron models, so it's an approximation running on top of real biological structure. What this opens up for you: The full open-source bridge code is on GitHub at Frankweb33/flybrain-robot-bridge.
bullets: Wire the brain to any robot using UDP motor commands over a network
Feed camera or sensor input as simulated sensory signals
Swap in your own robot, including a robot vacuum

news.headline: New looped transformer design gives language models unlimited reasoning depth
news.body: Normal AI models (transformers) have a fixed number of layers , like a stack of floors in a building. More thinking? You generate more tokens. That costs more money every time. The Recurrent Looped Transformer (RLT) flips this. Instead of a fixed stack, the model loops its layers across every token it processes, building a growing internal memory as the sequence gets longer. The reasoning depth scales with the sequence, not the architecture. Three things it targets: Important caveat: this is a design spec, not a tested product . Early experiments show mixed results, and the paper itself says efficiency and scaling gains need future validation. Worth watching, not shipping.
bullets: Deeper reasoning over time without generating extra tokens
Hardware-friendly design with parallel encoding and memory reuse
Cleaner AI training, where the model behaves the same during learning and real use

news.headline: Developer builds open-source Codex clone that runs on your existing ChatGPT plan
news.body: Codex is OpenAI's AI coding agent that works directly on your project files. Cool, but it has a separate usage limit. Once you hit it, you're stuck. Chat On Steroids flips that. It uses your regular ChatGPT conversation instead, so it does not consume your Codex quota at all. Same power, different bucket. Here's what you can actually do with it: To get started: install CoS, approve your project folder in Settings, then connect it through ChatGPT's Developer mode. Pairing is automatic. You need Windows, macOS, or Linux, plus Chrome or Edge with a ChatGPT account that supports Developer mode. The code is open source on GitHub.
bullets: Read and edit files directly in your project folder
Send corrections while work is still running
Split tasks across multiple agents working in parallel
Resume a session in a fresh chat without losing context
